events.category: Tokyo guitar-led crossover / live beatmaking-to-band experiment
events.factual_description: BLUES ALLEY JAPAN presents TANAKA YOSHITO LIVE EXPERIMENT IX on Thursday, November 5, 2026 at 1-3-14 Meguro, Meguro-ku, Tokyo, B1F of Meguro Holic Hotel. Doors are at 6:00 PM and the two-set performance begins at 7:00 PM. The announced lineup is Katsuyuki Mito on vocals/keyboards, Takashi Numazawa on drums, Tomohiko Ohkanda on bass, and Yoshito Tanaka on guitar/backing vocals. The venue lists advance prices of ¥6,500 for a table seat, ¥11,500 for a Plate Set, and ¥14,500 for a Dinner Set; same-day prices are ¥550 higher, and the table seat carries a separate ¥550 seat charge. BAJ Club advance reservations are scheduled to open September 9 at noon and general venue reservations September 16 at 2:00 PM. The authorized eplus event page describes Tanaka as a guitarist and sound producer and says the concert turns original material designed with MPC3000 and Ableton LIVE into vivid live music with this band.

en.why_it_matters: The hook is the conversion from studio architecture to a real band. Tanaka's solo language has been built from beatmaking, synth space and a very identifiable guitar voice; here material designed with MPC3000 and Ableton LIVE is handed to voice/keys, bass, drums and guitar and asked to breathe as live music. That makes the experiment less about watching a session guitarist stretch out and more about hearing programmed structure, groove and instrumental interaction negotiate with each other in a small Meguro room.
en.trip_verdict: If November 5 falls inside a Tokyo stay and the beatmaking-to-guitar thread sounds interesting, this is a worthwhile Meguro night to keep in the options. I would not break an already stronger plan or reroute a Kanto itinerary around it.

es.why_it_matters: El gancho está en pasar la arquitectura de estudio a una banda real. El lenguaje solista de Tanaka se ha construido con beatmaking, espacio de sintetizadores y una voz de guitarra muy reconocible; aquí material diseñado con MPC3000 y Ableton LIVE pasa a voz/teclados, bajo, batería y guitarra para respirar como música en vivo. El interés no es simplemente ver a un guitarrista de sesión soltarse, sino escuchar cómo la estructura programada, el groove y la interacción instrumental negocian entre sí en un cuarto pequeño de Meguro.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 5 de noviembre cae dentro de una estancia en Tokio y te interesa el cruce entre beatmaking y guitarra, vale tener esta noche de Meguro entre las opciones. No rompería un plan fuerte ya armado ni reordenaría un itinerario de Kanto alrededor de esta fecha.
